## Natural history notes

A small jumping spider characterized by its compact body, quick movements, and pale tan to brown coloration, often with darker markings on the body and legs. In Florida, it is commonly found on shrubs, palmettos, grasses, garden plants, forest edges, and other low vegetation where it actively searches for prey. It does not build a prey-capturing web; instead, it uses its strong vision and jumping ability to stalk and pounce on small insects and other arthropods, often resting on leaves or stems during the day.
